notes: The ATMS status is defeated and all three objections land on real seams in the original. The rebutting objection (tests i and iv contradict) is the sharpest: the original offered no way to distinguish a legitimate second check from fraud-shopping, and any fix seemed to violate iv. The refinement resolves it by narrowing iv from 'no shared data' to 'no shared attribute-level data' and permitting a minimal non-identifying fraud signal, with an explicit failure condition if that signal leaks attributes or query patterns. The undercutting objection (liability covers defective checks, not conduct) is accepted outright: test iii is split into the identity-fraud case (certifier pays) and the genuine-identity case (individual is nameable), and a SCOPE section states that conduct guarantees are a separate product. This shrinks the claim but makes it defensible. The undermining objection (eIDAS already does this) is largely conceded: the refined thesis drops the 'new architecture' framing and states three narrower additions, with an explicit fallback to 'deployment profile' if those too prove pre-existing. The unsupported assumptions about certifier supply and insurer appetite are surfaced in test v as conditions the thesis currently fails rather than silently relied on. The grading-neutrality assumption is addressed by requiring the grading body not to certify. The direction of the thesis — unbundle certifying, grading, and accepting so a small relying party can accept a stranger — is preserved throughout.
